Under the renewed NCIB, Wesdome may purchase for cancellation up to 7,187,337 common shares (the "

"), representing approximately 5% of the Company's public float of 143,309,909 shares as of October 30, 2026. Purchases may be made during the 12-month period commencing on November 9, 2026, and ending on the earlier of November 8, 2027, or the date on which the Company completes its purchases under the NCIB. As of October 30, 2026, Wesdome had 143,746,743 shares issued and outstanding.

Wesdome's board of directors believes that, from time to time, the market price of the Shares may not fully reflect the underlying value of the Company's business and prospects, and that the purchase of Shares under the NCIB is an appropriate use of the Company's available liquidity and is in the best interests of the Company and its shareholders. The Company will continue to be opportunistic in its approach to Share repurchases under the NCIB, subject to market conditions and other factors.

Purchases under the NCIB will be made through the facilities of the TSX or alternative Canadian trading systems at the prevailing market price at the time of purchase, in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements. In accordance with TSX rules, daily purchases on the TSX under the NCIB will be limited to 159,948 Shares, representing 25% of the average daily trading volume of 639,792 Shares on the TSX for the six months prior to October 30, 2026, subject to Wesdome's ability to make one block purchase of Shares per calendar week that exceeds such limits. All Shares purchased under the NCIB will be cancelled. Purchases will be funded from the Company's existing cash resources.

The actual number of Shares purchased under the NCIB, and the timing of any purchases, will be determined by management of the Company based on market conditions, share price, available cash resources and other opportunities to invest capital for growth. Wesdome is not obligated to purchase any Shares under the NCIB and may suspend or discontinue purchases at any time, subject to applicable laws.

Under the Company's current normal course issuer bid, which commenced on November 7, 2025, and expires on November 6, 2026, the Company was authorized to purchase up to 9,013,300 Shares and had purchased 7,833,800 Shares at a weighted average price of $24.4282 for a total of approximately $190 million as of November 4, 2026.
In connection with the renewed NCIB, the Company intends to renew its automatic share purchase plan (the "

") to allow for the purchase of Shares under the NCIB at times when the Company would ordinarily not be permitted to purchase Shares due to regulatory restrictions or internal trading blackout periods. Before entering a blackout period, the Company may, but is not required to, instruct NBF to make purchases under the NCIB based on parameters set by the Company in accordance with the ASPP, TSX rules and applicable securities laws. The ASPP has been pre-cleared by the TSX and is expected to take effect on November 9, 2026. Outside of blackout periods, Shares may be purchased under the NCIB at the discretion of management.

Wesdome is a Canadian-focused gold producer with two high-grade underground assets — the Eagle River mine in Ontario and the Kiena mine in Quebec. The Company's primary goal is to responsibly leverage its operating platform and high-quality brownfield and greenfield exploration pipeline to build a value-driven mid-tier Canadian gold producer.

This news release contains "forward-looking information" which may include, but is not limited to, statements with respect to the Company's NCIB and ASPP, the methods by which any such purchases will be made, the Company's beliefs and expectations regarding the NCIB, and other statements that are not historical facts. Purchases made under the NCIB will be subject to various factors, including Wesdome's capital and liquidity positions, accounting and regulatory considerations, financial and operational performance, alternative uses of capital, the trading price of the Shares, and general market conditions. The NCIB does not oblige Wesdome to acquire a specific dollar amount or number of shares and may be extended, modified, or discontinued at any time at Wesdome's discretion.
